Exercise Guide

Every movement in the plan, with an animated demo of the correct form. The figures loop like a GIF — watch the shape the body makes, then match it. Written cues matter more than speed: slow and controlled beats fast, every time.

The three core moves (curl-up, side plank, bird dog) are the McGill Big 3 — chosen specifically because they build core stiffness without bending or compressing the spine. That's the whole point given the disc history: brace, don't bend.

Curl-up (McGill)

  • Lie on your back. One knee bent, foot flat; the other leg straight.
  • Slide both hands under the arch of your low back — they're there to preserve the arch, not cushion it. Don't flatten your back into the floor.
  • Lift head and shoulders as one unit, just a few centimeters — imagine your head resting on a bathroom scale and you're taking the weight off it.
  • No chin poke, no crunching. If your low back moves, you went too high.
  • Hold about 8 seconds, breathing normally. Lower slowly. Swap legs halfway through your sets.
  • Week 1 dose: 5 per side.

Why this one: it trains the abs isometrically with zero spinal flexion — a crunch without the crunch. Loaded spinal flexion is permanently off the menu (rule 1); this is the substitute, straight from the spine-rehab literature.

Side plank, from knees

  • Lie on your side, propped on your forearm. Elbow directly under the shoulder — this stacks the joint so the arm just holds position, it doesn't press. That matters for the left-arm rule.
  • Knees bent to about 90°, one on top of the other.
  • Drive your hips up until shoulder–hip–knee make a straight line. Don't let the hips sag back down or roll forward.
  • Hold, breathing normally, then lower with control. Do both sides.
  • Left side caution: you're supporting on the left forearm when the left side is down. The elbow-under-shoulder position keeps the arm short and stacked — that's allowed. If the pec-to-elbow line lights up at all, the set ends immediately (rule 2).
  • Week 1 dose: 10-second holds per side.

Bird dog

  • Hands and knees. Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat like a table.
  • Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back, both to horizontal. The goal is a straight line from fingertips to heel.
  • The hard part is what doesn't move: hips stay level, back stays flat, no arching or twisting. Imagine balancing a cup of coffee on your low back.
  • Hold a few seconds, return with control, switch sides.
  • Left arm note: reaching forward with a straight arm is fine here — the arm is unloaded (nothing in the hand, no pressing). If it ever complains, point the thumb up and reach a little less far, or just extend the leg only.
  • Week 1 dose: 5 per side.

Glute bridge

  • Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat about hip-width, arms relaxed at your sides.
  • Squeeze your glutes and push through your heels to lift the hips until shoulders–hips–knees form a straight line.
  • Stop at straight. Lifting higher just cranks the low back — the glutes are done working at the top.
  • Pause a second at the top, lower with control.
  • This is the staple for the hips and hamstrings (rule 4) — it strengthens them with zero spinal load. Stop each set 3–4 reps short of grinding.
  • Week 1 dose: 2×10.

Incline push-up

  • Hands on a sturdy counter, table, or wall-bar at about chest height, slightly wider than shoulders.
  • Walk your feet back until your body is a straight line from head to heels. Brace like a plank — no sagging hips.
  • Lower your chest to the surface, elbows tracking about 45° from your body (not flared straight out), then press back to straight arms.
  • Left arm rules apply hard here (rule 2): keep the press close to the body, never lock out hard into a fully extended reach, and the instant the pec-to-elbow line lights up, the set is over. The steeper the incline, the lighter the load — steeper is always the right call in doubt.
  • Week 1 dose: 2×8.

Chair-assisted squat

  • Stand in front of a sturdy chair, feet about shoulder-width.
  • Push your hips back first — like reaching your butt for the seat — then bend the knees. Arms reach forward as a counterweight.
  • Lower with control until you lightly tap the chair. Tap, don't sit. If a rep is failing, sitting down fully is the built-in safety net — that's why the chair is there.
  • Stand back up by driving through your heels and squeezing your glutes.
  • Keep the chest up; the torso leans forward naturally but the back stays neutral, never rounded (rule 1 — no loaded spinal flexion).
  • Week 1 dose: 2×8.

The cardio (no demo needed)

  • Walking: brisk enough that you're breathing deeper but can still talk in full sentences. Compression shorts + anti-chafe balm every time (rule 3).
  • Elliptical: conversational pace. If you can't speak a sentence, slow down — the aerobic base that eventually bikes across America is built at easy pace, not by suffering. Same skin protocol as walking.
